reaction.notes: Step A only: acetylation of 6-bromobenzothiophene with acetyltrimethylsilane using Pd(PPh3)4 and CsF in 1,2-dichloroethane at 75 °C for 24 h under inert atmosphere.
reaction.tags: palladium; aryl bromide; acetylation; silyl enol; cesium fluoride; 1,2-dichloroethane; argon

conditions.atmosphere: Set up under argon; purge 5 min
Inert (argon) with air condenser; oil bath; vigorous stirring (≈800 rpm)

workup: Cool to 23 °C; dilute with heptane (75 mL).
Filter through silica plug (≈50 g; pre-wet with EtOAc 100 mL); elute with EtOAc (≈500 mL).

purification.fractions: Collect 25 mL fractions; pool product-containing fractions (per TLC).

notes: TLC: 9:1 hexanes:EtOAc; SM Rf ≈ 0.73 (UV), product Rf ≈ 0.32 (p-anisaldehyde, UV).
Authors note nitrogen also used successfully; main text describes argon positive pressure.

original_procedure: Flame-dry a 250 mL round-bottom flask, cool under inert gas, and charge with 6-bromobenzothiophene, CsF, and Pd(PPh3)4. Purge (~5 min), then add acetyltrimethylsilane followed by 1,2-dichloroethane. Fit a reflux condenser and heat at 75 °C with vigorous stirring under inert atmosphere for 24 h. Allow to cool, dilute with heptane, filter through a silica plug (EtOAc elution), concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography (heptane/EtOAc gradient) to obtain 6-acetylbenzothiophene (Step A, paraphrased; see source URL for full text).
